lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.title: Application or project: noticing hazards early

standardsRefs: Ready for Life v1, Grade 4 Unit 1: Home Care Routines That Last
Manuel Academy local Ready for Life composition
objective: I can practice noticing hazards early. I will do one step at a time and check one result.
scenario: A trusted adult agrees to a hazard walk-through of one shared space in the household, such as a hallway, stairwell, or main living area.
safetyNotes: A trusted adult walks through the space together with the learner for the entire hazard walk-through.
The learner points out or describes each hazard but never touches, moves, plugs in, unplugs, or attempts to fix anything themselves.
If a hazard involves electricity, water near an outlet, or a blocked exit, the learner steps back and lets the adult handle it immediately rather than finishing the rest of the walk-through first.

simulationAlternative.description: If a real walk-through isn't possible right now, the learner instead studies a printed or hand-drawn floor plan of a household space, real or one they know well, and marks three specific spots where a hazard like a trip risk, a blocked exit, or an unsecured item could realistically occur, explaining the urgency rating they would give each one.

materials: adult-or-local: one real shared space to walk through
learner-local: paper or a notes app for recording hazards and urgency ratings

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g4-u01-l04-model-card. Watch one complete example.

prompts.text: Name the first move in the model and explain why it comes first.

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g4-u01-l04-guided-card. Do the coached move.

prompts.text: Name the move you completed and the success check it meets.

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g4-u01-l04-independent-card. Choose one complete route. Follow its steps.

prompts.text: Which complete route did you use?
Record the completed step numbers and one non-sensitive result statement.

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g4-u01-l04-evidence-record. Save one result and one reflection.

prompts.text: Explain why rating a hazard's urgency and reporting it right away matters more than waiting until the hazard causes an actual injury, using the highest-urgency hazard you found as your example.

remediation: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g4-u01-l04-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step. Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g4-u01-l04-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check. Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments. Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g4-u01-l04-retry-pair without the coach prompt. Exit: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Hazard identification specificity: At least three specific hazards are named with an exact location for each. | Safe reporting behavior: The learner points out and reports every hazard to the adult without handling it directly. Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g4-u01-l04-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.
extension: Have the learner repeat the hazard walk-through in a second shared space and compare the two spaces' highest-urgency hazard, explaining which space needs attention sooner and why.

resources.title: noticing hazards early worked model
resources.purpose: Shows the starting condition, visible moves, reasoning, and success check before the learner begins.
content: Starting condition: A trusted adult agrees to a hazard walk-through of one shared space in the household, such as a hallway, stairwell, or main living area.
Model move 1: Read the condition and name the exact noticing hazards early decision or action.
Model move 2: Before walking through the space, think about what kinds of hazards you already know to look for.
Model move 3: With your adult, walk through the shared space slowly and point out anything that could cause a fall, burn, cut, or other injury, without touching it.

Model check: Hazard identification specificity: At least three specific hazards are named with an exact location for each. | Safe reporting behavior: The learner points out and reports every hazard to the adult without handling it directly.

resources.title: noticing hazards early action steps
resources.purpose: Provides the ordered directions used by the model, guided attempt, independent task, and retry.
content: 1. Read the goal for noticing hazards early.
2. Watch the worked move on swk-rfl-g4-u01-l04-model-card.
3. Do one coached move on swk-rfl-g4-u01-l04-guided-card.
4. Complete the chosen route on swk-rfl-g4-u01-l04-independent-card.
5. Save the small record on swk-rfl-g4-u01-l04-evidence-record; use swk-rfl-g4-u01-l04-retry-pair if a step is missed.

resources.title: noticing hazards early coached first attempt
resources.purpose: Carries the complete first attempt and a fresh correction turn.
content: Fictional practice condition: A trusted adult agrees to a hazard walk-through of one shared space in the household, such as a hallway, stairwell, or main living area.
Coach direction: Before walking through the space, think about what kinds of hazards you already know to look for.
Learner prompt: List three types of hazards you already know how to spot, such as something you could trip on, something hot, or something blocking a door.
Feedback check: name the move completed, point to the matching success check, and identify one missing or uncertain step without judging the learner.
Fresh correction turn: use the same fictional condition with one constraint changed; restate the changed constraint, redo only the affected step, and check the new result.

resources.title: noticing hazards early complete application
resources.purpose: Contains the lesson-specific application directions and prompts; it is the delivered card referenced by the learner flow.
content: Application direction: With your adult, walk through the shared space slowly and point out anything that could cause a fall, burn, cut, or other injury, without touching it.
Response 1 (t2-p1): I pointed out or described each hazard out loud instead of touching, moving, or fixing it myself.
Response 2 (t2-p2): I found at least three specific hazards, not vague ones like 'it's messy.'
Response 3 (t2-p3): My adult confirmed or corrected each hazard I pointed out before we moved to the next one.

Equal-access rule: If a real walk-through isn't possible right now, the learner instead studies a printed or hand-drawn floor plan of a household space, real or one they know well, and marks three specific spots where a hazard like a trip risk, a blocked exit, or an unsecured item could realistically occur, explaining the urgency rating they would give each one.

resources.title: noticing hazards early minimal evidence record
resources.purpose: Defines exactly what the learner saves and what must not be collected.
content: Record only: selected route, completed step numbers, one non-sensitive result statement, and one revision if a step changed.

Reflection: Explain why rating a hazard's urgency and reporting it right away matters more than waiting until the hazard causes an actual injury, using the highest-urgency hazard you found as your example.

Success checks: Hazard identification specificity: At least three specific hazards are named with an exact location for each. | Safe reporting behavior: The learner points out and reports every hazard to the adult without handling it directly.
Do not collect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations; account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details; photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules.

resources.title: noticing hazards early supported and parallel retry cards
resources.purpose: Delivers a real correction loop rather than a direction to try again without support.
content: Contrast reteach: compare the model check on swk-rfl-g4-u01-l04-model-card with the missed or unsupported step; name the one observable difference.
Supported card: return to swk-rfl-g4-u01-l04-guided-card, complete the affected move with one coach prompt, and receive criterion-specific feedback.
Parallel card: use a fresh fictional noticing hazards early condition with one changed constraint; complete the same move without the coach prompt.

Exit check: the corrected move meets this lesson's checks — Hazard identification specificity: At least three specific hazards are named with an exact location for each. | Safe reporting behavior: The learner points out and reports every hazard to the adult without handling it directly..
Return: resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g4-u01-l04-independent-card; a physical route resumes only when the authorized adult says it is safe.

retry.trigger: Start the correction loop when a required step is missing, the reason does not match the condition, a safety or privacy boundary is crossed, or the evidence does not show the stated result.
retry.targetedReteach: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g4-u01-l04-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step.
retry.supportedReattempt: Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g4-u01-l04-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check.
retry.feedback: Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments.
retry.parallelReattempt: Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g4-u01-l04-retry-pair without the coach prompt.
retry.exitCriterion: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Hazard identification specificity: At least three specific hazards are named with an exact location for each. | Safe reporting behavior: The learner points out and reports every hazard to the adult without handling it directly.

guardianInvolvement.role: Give permission; provide only the supervision, handling, review, or observation named in the lesson; attest only that the physical event occurred.
guardianInvolvement.signOffBoundary: A guardian attestation certifies only that the named physical event occurred. It never scores the learner reflection or proves effort, honesty, maturity, responsibility, diagnosis, or character.

safety.stopRule: Stop the physical route when permission, supervision, a safe setting, or an expected material is missing, or when a new hazard appears. Continue only when the authorized adult resolves it; otherwise use the complete fictional route.
safety.physicalBoundary: The learner follows the source safety notes and never performs adult-only handling, transport, account, legal, medical, heat, sharp-tool, electrical, chemical, or machine actions.
safety.noShameRule: Describe only the observable step, condition, evidence, or revision. Never label the learner, household, body, ability, effort, maturity, responsibility, or character.

privacy.rule: Collect the smallest process record that shows the lesson steps. A learner may choose fictional details and may decline private disclosure without losing credit.

photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules

may: coach the guided and retry cards
mayNot: observe or claim a physical condition
tutorBoundary.physicalCompletionRule: Tutor or AI may coach. Tutor or AI may not certify that a real-world physical action occurred.
tutorBoundary.missingResourceAction: Stop and name the unresolved resource. Do not fabricate it; use another complete delivered route only when every resource for that route resolves.
